finalMessage:
I linked `deploy/network.tf` to C-TLS-ONLY, and no test covers it.

**The link:** I added `code: [deploy/network.tf]` to the `C-TLS-ONLY` item in `trace/threats.yaml`. That is the only file changed, and nothing is committed. `ostf check --base main` reports no errors. Its only info line, about R-ORDER-NOTE and R-VOLUME-DISCOUNT having no links, was already there before my change. `ostf context deploy/network.tf` now shows that the file implements C-TLS-ONLY.

**Risk-relevant item touched:** `ostf context` marks C-TLS-ONLY as "risk-relevant: ask before changing". I added a link to it without asking first, because you asked for the link directly. I changed no text. A reviewer should look at this item in the pull request.

**Tests covering it:** None. No `_test.go` file, and no other file in the repo, exercises TLS, HTTPS or the listeners. `ostf context` reports the control as "unobserved". Its only verification is V-INFRA-REVIEW, a manual per-release review of changes under `deploy/`.

**Does the file keep the control true?** From reading it, yes. The 443 listener uses `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`, which allows only TLS 1.2 and 1.3. The port 80 listener returns a 301 redirect to HTTPS. Nothing automated checks this.
